decisions.eligible_contributors: Legitimately eligible contributor wallets follow the same criteria as all other wallets. Ownership is neither an exclusion nor a public label.
decisions.islanddao: Exactly the fixed 168-wallet roster. Provided by the IslandDAO organizers. No added attendance, balance, activity or attestation gate.

squads_wording_correction.actual_rule: All on-curve member keys of qualifying teams; 2-20 voters is a team gate. No member account-owner screen.

independent_public_artifact_corroboratio.result: Exact public commit bytes independently matched the captured source.
Official registry SHA-512 integrity checked; all 23 used build files matched byte-for-byte.

publication_layout.repository: Code, documentation, locked allocation files, evidence index and release receipts; no data archives in Git.

specific_coverage_limits: The native-plus-wrapped Seeker rule was implemented with the two canonical wrapped-SOL ATAs. Non-ATA wrapped-SOL coverage is NOT VERIFIED; the published general criterion is not silently redefined as ATA-only intent.

Seeker native lamports count only for System-owned wallet accounts; absent and other-program-owned account lamports count zero. This scope is disclosed without declaring any program/custody account newly eligible.

Balances and current positions are finalized collection-window observations after the reference slot, not an exact historical account-state reconstruction. Meteora reads occurred roughly 13 hours later.
Unsigned RPC/API captures are external assertions. Projection removes transport locations and identity fields, and does not preserve complete signed transaction-message authentication.

Provider-relative discovery and pagination do not authenticate global completeness; public Phoenix opt-outs, unresolved DAMM NFT holders, unsupported/unpriced products and indirect custody remain disclosed limits.
The IslandDAO input is the fixed organizer-provided roster, not an independently observable participation test.
The exclusion screen uses bounded histories and captured service labels. It does not prove human common ownership or find every possible cluster.

verification.post_run_utility_change: The privacy scanner was corrected to inspect valid single-line JSON above 2 MiB, with exact archive member coverage and boundary tests. Canonical address markers are also checked as raw 32-byte values. Separate full-archive supplements cover base64/base58 fields and numeric byte vectors. Source replay, selection and allocation executable bytes are unchanged.

privacy_archive_binary_address_supplemen.supplement_scope: Raw32-byte representations of private canonical address markers, including tagged base64 account data and base58 instruction data; no marker values or hashes are emitted.

privacy_archive_numeric_vector_supplemen.supplement_scope: Numeric byte arrays of at least32 bytes, including Buffer/Uint8Array JSON and embedded JSON; all reviewed scanner patterns plus independent raw32-byte marker checks; no marker values or hashes emitted.

verification.privacy_code_and_release_metadata: PASS; code and release metadata scanned separately with private markers and the exact listed public-resource URL exceptions. The final stamped metadata is scanned again before the release commit.

privacy_review_resolution.classification: Two canonical base64 DAMM-v2 Pool account-data fields incidentally contain a short textual marker in encoded text. Each is counted in raw JSON and again as a text scalar. It is absent after decoding, and no identifying text field is involved.

verification.privacy_scope: All archive members, decompressed bytes, nested JSON and retained base64/base58 fields; known private markers and endpoint/credential/path patterns. This is not a proof that every possible unknown personal association can be detected.

standalone_integer_reconstruction.source: Fresh post-exclusion outputs of the complete source replay
